# 30s product context

This is the canonical product overlay for PARA-managed 30s work. It applies
when the task explicitly concerns the 30s car application in
`quocchungthan/internet-facing` (`web/`) or its approved planning scope in
[Project 15](https://github.com/users/quocchungthan/projects/15/views/2),
Service **CarMaintaince**. It does not apply to unrelated services in that
repository or to PARA Bridge product decisions.

## Approved long-term goal

Help car owners understand their selected vehicle and make evidence-backed
maintenance decisions, growing from useful engine-first learning to honest
full-car coverage without unsupported diagnosis or unsafe instructions.

Changing this goal requires an explicit human decision. New evidence can
change the next increment without changing the goal.

## Product backbone: visual first

Detailed car drawings and interaction are the primary experience. Information,
teaching and guidance attach to the visible subject; they are not a replacement
for delivering the drawing. This owner direction supersedes the earlier
information-only primary-pilot recommendation.

Prioritize recognizable, meaningful component detail and correct installed
relationships over decorative visual polish. The drawing, component index and
search results must resolve to the same canonical selected-car subject: finding
a part highlights/focuses it, and selecting it reveals the matching index entry
and explanation. A result without drawable coverage must state that limit,
not highlight an unrelated mesh or promise a nonexistent part.

Start with one bounded detailed visual system, engine-first unless owner
priority changes, rather than modeling the whole car before testing usefulness.
Acceptance includes recognizable parts, meaningful selection boundaries,
index/search-to-subject consistency and attached teaching. Fidelity/accuracy
must be declared and supported; more polygons alone do not prove useful detail.
Keyboard/index access and text fallback remain essential alternatives, but an
information-only fallback does not satisfy this primary visual increment.

## Product Owner participation

Use the [Product Owner role](../agents/product-owner.agent.md) at 30s task
intake for a bug or feature, when review/research/experiment evidence changes
an assumption, and before backlog reprioritization or a release-scope decision.
Record the product-impact note in the current task/report. Read this context
and the role even when the user did not explicitly mention a Product Owner.

A bounded review can be performed in the current authorized session using
that role's guidance; it does not require another process for every ticket.
If separate managed review is justified, use the coordinator's approved,
self-contained request and normal protocol ownership/approval gates.
These instructions do not register an automatic runtime hook or make an
open attended CLI resume itself. Other repositories do not acquire these
instructions merely because PARA refers to them.

The Product Owner may publish tickets and reprioritize within **explicitly
approved 30s planning batches**. Outside the approved batch, propose changes.
Experiments are proposals only until separately approved for execution.
Do not let a recurring review expand its own read/write or publication scope.

## Stable product constraints

- Engine-first: choose one useful visual owner task, deliver one accepted
  interactive drawing slice with attached teaching, observe usefulness, then
  choose the next increment.
  ENG02 and CAT05 are the same package outcome, not separate delivery credit.
- Domain inclusion and experience capabilities are independent dimensions.
  A fuel tank, battery, engine or brake explanation is domain growth;
  selection, learning, rendering and reviewed guidance are separate
  capabilities. Flags restrict what exists; they create neither content,
  geometry, evidence nor authorization.
- Preserve the approved workshop layout and existing components. Use truthful
  partial/unknown/excluded/error states. Learning does not require geometry.
  Full-car coverage means a declared honest coverage index, not every OEM part.
- Keep manual/static accepted input viable. Future apps and AI use the same
  versioned validation, provenance and publication boundary. Contributor
  attestation is not independent certification; screenshots do not prove facts.
- Technical identity includes applicable market/configuration/source scope;
  appearance does not establish fitment. Original factory references and
  current installed configuration can differ. Exact repair procedures need
  separately qualified applicability/safety review.
- Keep coffee support and car requests separate. No donation buys priority
  or delivery guarantees. Respect request privacy and truthful fulfillment.
- External integrations, AI loops, whole-car completeness and later domains
  are evidence-led options, not automatic prerequisites for the first useful
  visual slice. Required drawing detail and interaction are core, not optional.

## Backlog balance and prioritization

At a bounded backlog review, identify physical-system/content increments
separately from shared user-facing capabilities, enabling work and reference/
planning cards. Report both all-card and work-ticket denominators where useful;
exclude parent rollups from leaf counts and flag shared outcomes explicitly.
Counts are not effort percentages or evidence of completed functionality.

Prefer owner-visible drawing/detail/interaction increments and the information
attached to them once their necessary foundations are ready. Keep essential
safety, rights, quality and recovery gates, but challenge
speculative infrastructure and repeated planning that delays learning.
Do not create filler tickets or enforce an arbitrary fixed domain percentage.
Uncovered concrete subjects such as a battery need an owner question, applicable
source and explicit scope, not an assumption that a broad category is complete.

The owner requires the active delivery plan to contain more concrete
owner-visible car increments than enabler/technical tasks. Show that active
slice explicitly, count unique leaf outcomes rather than parent/reference
cards, and expose prerequisites separately. Do not claim that the historical
all-card backlog already meets this balance or manufacture tickets to meet it.
Enrich existing system stories with concrete drawable component outcomes;
use new tickets only for distinct useful increments.

Research must progressively enrich the car itself: sourced component purpose,
relationships, recognizable drawing boundaries, selection/index/search labels
and attached teaching. Feed small dependency-ordered implementation examples
and focused checks into the same tickets. Keep future model handoffs bounded;
reference code is not proof of actual car geometry or completed application work.

Use actual owner priority and pilot evidence to decide the next system;
do not infer demand from the number of cards. Record priority changes and
tradeoffs in the existing canonical items/map. Dates remain provisional
planning-focus forecasts unless capacity and execution commitments are
explicitly established. Do not overwrite dates without explaining the change.
